plan.summary: This 1-4 block is a simple off-camp strength and power build for boxing with one weekly bodyweight-only session. Week 1 establishes a baseline on the main lower-body strength pattern so later work can be compared, and the main training starts in Week 2. With only one S&C day each week, the session stays full-body and focused on explosive intent, clean reps, and recoverable strength work that will not interfere too much with boxing practice.

phaseOverview.label: Building
phaseOverview.focus: Build basic full-body strength and low-impact power with simple bodyweight work done fast and clean.

phaseOverview.label: Intensifying
phaseOverview.focus: Make the main bodyweight strength work harder through tempo, range, and unilateral progressions while keeping jump quality high.

phaseOverview.label: Expressing
phaseOverview.focus: Keep strength with lower volume and express it through faster jumps, throws-by-intent, and sharper explosive push work.

exercises.name: Countermovement Jump
exercises.notes: Jump as high as you can on each rep. Land softly and reset fully between reps.

substitutionOptions.name: Squat Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if you need a simpler jump with less rhythm.

substitutionOptions.name: Pogo Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if jump tolerance is low and you need the lowest-impact option.

exercises.name: Split Squat
exercises.notes: Use a controlled descent and full range. This top set establishes your baseline for future progress on the main lower-body strength pattern.

strengthAssessment.prompt: Warm up with easy bodyweight sets, then build to one hard set of 5 reps per side with the hardest clean variation you can perform. Use setup changes like tempo, longer range, or rear-foot elevation to make it challenging, and log exactly what you used.

performanceTarget.prompt: Track the hardest clean 5-rep set per side and note the variation used.

substitutionOptions.name: Rear-Foot-Elevated Split Squat
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if regular split squats are too easy and balance is still solid.

substitutionOptions.name: Reverse Lunge
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if split squats bother the front knee.

exercises.name: Push-Up
exercises.notes: Use a straight body line and pause briefly at the bottom. Stop each set with 1-2 clean reps still in reserve.

performanceTarget.prompt: Track your best clean set without losing body position.

substitutionOptions.name: Incline Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if floor push-ups are not yet clean for the target reps.

substitutionOptions.name: Close-Grip Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if regular push-ups are too easy and elbows feel good.

exercises.name: Bodyweight Row Under Table or Bar
exercises.notes: Pull the chest toward the edge or bar and keep the body rigid. Stop before form breaks.

substitutionOptions.name: Doorframe Row
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if you have no stable low bar or table setup.

substitutionOptions.name: Towel Row Isometric
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if dynamic rows are not possible. Pull hard for a full effort hold.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Glute Bridge
exercises.notes: Drive through the heel and finish with the hips fully extended without arching the low back.

substitutionOptions.name: Two-Leg Glute Bridge
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if single-leg work cramps or feels unstable.

substitutionOptions.name: Hamstring Walkout
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if you want a harder posterior-chain option without equipment.

exercises.name: Hollow Body Hold
exercises.notes: Keep ribs down and low back lightly pressed toward the floor. Shorten the lever if you lose position.

substitutionOptions.name: Dead Bug
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if hollow holds are too hard to keep clean.

substitutionOptions.name: V-Sit Tuck Hold
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if you want a harder trunk flexion hold.

exercises.name: Front Neck Isometric Against Hand
exercises.notes: Use gentle steady pressure and keep the neck long. This should feel like light to moderate work, not grinding.

substitutionOptions.name: Side Neck Isometric Against Hand
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if you want to rotate the neck emphasis week to week.

exercises.name: Countermovement Jump
exercises.notes: Every rep should look springy and sharp. Stop if jump height clearly drops.

substitutionOptions.name: Squat Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if you need a simpler takeoff.

substitutionOptions.name: Pogo Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if impact tolerance is low.

exercises.name: Split Squat
exercises.notes: Use the hardest variation you can control cleanly. Move down under control and drive up hard.

performanceTarget.prompt: Track the hardest clean set and keep the variation consistent unless it becomes too easy.

substitutionOptions.name: Rear-Foot-Elevated Split Squat
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if standard split squats are too easy.

substitutionOptions.name: Reverse Lunge
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if split squats are uncomfortable on the hips or knees.

exercises.name: Push-Up
exercises.notes: Explode up without losing body line. If you cannot keep clean reps, raise the hands and stay crisp.

performanceTarget.prompt: Track your best clean set at this rep range.

substitutionOptions.name: Incline Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if the floor version is too difficult.

substitutionOptions.name: Close-Grip Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if regular push-ups are too easy.

exercises.name: Bodyweight Row Under Table or Bar
exercises.notes: Keep shoulders down and pull the chest to the support each rep. Adjust body angle to stay in a clean range.

substitutionOptions.name: Doorframe Row
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if no stable row setup is available.

substitutionOptions.name: Towel Row Isometric
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if you need a safe no-equipment pulling option.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Glute Bridge

substitutionOptions.name: Two-Leg Glute Bridge

substitutionOptions.name: Hamstring Walkout

exercises.notes: Lift with control and avoid swinging. Keep the lower back from arching hard off the floor.

substitutionOptions.name: Hollow Body Hold
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if raises are too hard to control.

substitutionOptions.name: Reverse Crunch

exercises.name: Side Neck Isometric Against Hand
exercises.notes: Press gradually and keep the jaw relaxed. Stay smooth and controlled.

substitutionOptions.name: Front Neck Isometric Against Hand
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if side loading feels awkward.

exercises.name: Countermovement Jump
exercises.notes: Keep the contacts clean and the effort high. Rest enough so every set stays explosive.

substitutionOptions.name: Squat Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if countermovement timing gets messy.

substitutionOptions.name: Low Box Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if you have a safe stable surface and want a lower-landing option.

exercises.name: Rear-Foot-Elevated Split Squat
exercises.notes: Use full range and stay balanced over the front foot. Drive up hard without bouncing off the bottom.

substitutionOptions.name: Split Squat

substitutionOptions.name: Reverse Lunge
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if rear-foot elevation irritates the hips.

performanceTarget.prompt: Track your best clean set with the chosen foot height.

substitutionOptions.name: Push-Up

substitutionOptions.name: Close-Grip Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if you need a hard push-up variation without elevating the feet.

substitutionOptions.name: Pogo Jump

substitutionOptions.name: Close-Grip Push-Up
